# $LEMON (Lemon Brothers)

> $LEMON is a memecoin that can have a bank run. Every LEMON lives in one bank contract on NEAR testnet. Depositors
> who take their money out force the bank to sell loans at a loss, and those coins burn; when the bank falls, a
> rescue prints new ones. An AI model in a TEE holds the bank's chair inside limits the contract enforces. A browser
> game puts a person in the same chair, and its scores are checked by replay.

## Status

- Hackathon project built at NEAR HACKATHON. Tracks: `memecoins` (primary), `games`, `security`.
- NEAR testnet only. $LEMON is a test coin with no price. Not audited.
- Contract (token and bank): `lemonbank-587f5c93.testnet`, source `contracts/lemon-bank` and `contracts/bank-core`.
- Code on chain: sha256 `1559b5eb68480b28d37366dd798e303295f4cfc24e0839ec2549a81e6754b71e`.
- Owner: Sputnik DAO `lemon-brothers-587f5c93.sputnik-v2.testnet` (three test accounts, 2 of 3).
- The contract account holds no access key (the last one was deleted in transaction
  `BC31BkL3HF9vjdqeQe3iispk3KYFudAiTfTQwxKitDb9`): nobody can replace the code, the ceiling or the length of a bank day.
- Chair: `lemonhawk-24e23cdf.testnet`, model `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` on NEAR AI Cloud.
- The same team lead also submits QUEUE, an independent project with no shared code (hackathon rule Q-015).
- License: MIT.

## What is real and what is a game

- Real, on chain: the coin, the bank, deposits and withdrawals, the chair's signed policies, the supply log, the
  leaderboard's claims. "My coins" and "The bank, live" on the page act on and read this bank.
- A game, in the browser: "Play" (ten days as the chair) and the town mode run a TypeScript copy of the bank's rules
  (`packages/sim`). The copy never moves a real coin. Only a finished game's score goes on chain.
- The copy and the contract are kept identical by a parity test: 8,000 random operations, same state at every step.

## Rules that move the supply (constants in `contracts/bank-core/src/lib.rs`, explained in `RULES.md`)

- Burn: 40% of every loan sold to pay a withdrawal the vault cannot cover (`HAIRCUT_PERMILLE = 400`); loan
  write-offs; speech fee 10, rumour fee 25; the early-withdrawal fee.
- Print: loan yield 0.60% of the loan book per bank day; the chair's mint, at most 5% of supply per bank day and 15%
  per round; a rescue after a collapse, 20% of what the bank owed (`BAILOUT_PERMILLE = 200`); insurance payouts;
  1,000 LEMON once for a new account.
- Ceiling: no mint of any kind lifts the supply above `max_supply`. A new bank's ceiling is its opening supply plus
  a quarter; the testnet bank's is sealed at 150,000 LEMON. The game's copy is another bank with its own ceiling.
- A bank day lasts 55 minutes. Anyone may call `advance_epoch` once it has elapsed.

## Verify (all read-only unless stated)

| Command | Needs | Expect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `npm ci && npm run verify` | Node 22+, Rust (toolchain pinned in `contracts/rust-toolchain.toml`) | 183 TypeScript tests, then `test result: ok` for 14, 1 and 65 Rust tests, then the page builds; exit 0 |
| `npm run verify:chain` | Node, network | 53 `PASS` lines, `verify:chain: 53 checks passed, 0 failed` |
| `npm run verify:deployed` | Rust, network, an Apple-silicon Mac (the build host; on Linux it prints "NOT COMPARABLE HERE", and the hourly `testnet` workflow runs it on macOS) | `verify:deployed: OK: ... byte for byte` |
| `npm run monitor` | Node, network | seven `ok` lines, exit 0 |
| `npm run attack` | Node | `All five attempts were refused` |
| `npm run attest -- --file` | Node | `all checks passed` (Intel TDX quote chain of the saved NEAR AI attestation report) |
| `npm run dev` | Node | the page at http://127.0.0.1:5190 |

`npm run verify:chain` fetches every transaction listed in `apps/web/src/chain/evidence.json` and checks its signer,
its outcome and the quoted text. No script named above needs a key or sends a transaction.

## Limits (stated in README, "Status and limits" and "Key limits")

- Testnet only; the DAO council is three test accounts of the team. The chair and agent accounts keep their own
  full-access keys next to the limited ones; none of them can change the bank's code or rules.
- The contract verifies the model's signature against a key pinned from NEAR AI's attestation report; it does not
  verify the Intel quote itself (`npm run attest` does that off chain).
- The game's simulation runs in the browser; the contract stores score claims and cannot check them. Every browser,
  and `npm run verify:chain`, checks them by replay.
- The sixty depositors of the game are deterministic programs. AI depositors exist in a live local town and ran on
  testnet for seven bank days (docs/TESTNET.md, section 7).

## Files

- `README.md`: what it is, "do X, see Y" steps, how NEAR is used, limits.
- `RULES.md`: every rule and number, with the reason for each.
- `docs/TESTNET.md`: what ran on testnet, with transactions.
- `contracts/bank-core`: the bank's rules in pure Rust. `contracts/lemon-bank`: the NEAR contract.
- `packages/sim`: the TypeScript copy of the rules, the depositors, the game. `apps/web`: the page.
- `services/chair`: the NEAR AI client and signature checks. `scripts/`: verification, testnet tools.
